info.title: API.SH: Crunchbase
info.description: The Crunchbase API from API.SH: public Crunchbase data as clean JSON. Every endpoint is a GET with query parameters and your key in the x-api-key header. Calls that run cost the credits shown (x-credits): successes, and lookups that found nothing (404). Refused calls and errors on our side are free. Docs: https://api.sh/docs · Every platform: https://api.sh/openapi.json

get.description:
A company's Crunchbase profile as a logged-out visitor sees it: name, legal name, logo, short and full description, website, social links, company email and phone, categories and industries, headquarters and location groups, operating and IPO status, company type, employee range, tags (e.g. unicorn), founders, key people with titles, Crunchbase rank and its 90-day change, last funding type, and counts of funding rounds, investors, investments, acquisitions and sub-organizations. Then the lists the page shows (up to 10 entries each, the site's logged-out limit): funding rounds with type, investor count and lead investors; investors with the round they joined; investments; acquisitions; sub-organizations; exits; similar companies; products; recent news; key employee changes, layoffs, partnerships, product launches, awards and legal proceedings with their press sources; technologies used, apps with downloads and monthly web visits. Logged out, Crunchbase hides money amounts and most dates: `hidden_logged_out` names the fields it hid. `cards` keeps every section of the page as the site returns it.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/crunchbase-organization

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The organization's Crunchbase name (the part after /organization/ in its link), e.g. `stripe`, or a crunchbase.com/organization/... link.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
People with a Crunchbase profile (founders, executives, investors) whose name matches, best match first: name, Crunchbase name (`permalink`, the `id` for /crunchbase/v1/person), link, photo, headline (job title and organization), short description and the profile's sections; `total` when the site gives one.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/crunchbase-people-search

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
A founder's, executive's or investor's Crunchbase profile as a logged-out visitor sees it: name, photo, headline, description, primary job title and organization, location (city, region, country), LinkedIn/X/Facebook/website links the profile lists, investor types, rank, counts (current jobs, founded and portfolio organizations, investments, advisor roles, event appearances, news), current and past jobs, board and advisory roles, education, investments (at most 10 logged out, money and dates hidden), partner investments, exits, event appearances, recent news and lists the person appears in. No personal contact details.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/crunchbase-person

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The person's Crunchbase name (e.g. `patrick-collison`) or the crunchbase.com/person/... link.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
Organizations whose name matches, as the Crunchbase search box suggests them (best match first): name, Crunchbase name (`id` for /crunchbase/v1/organization), link, logo, short description and the data sections the profile has; plus how many organizations match in total (`total`, null when the site does not say). `type=investors` lists investment firms only.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/crunchbase-search

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

apiKey.name: x-api-key
apiKey.description: Create keys at https://app.api.sh/keys. Authorization: Bearer <key> also works.

raw.name: raw
raw.description: 0 leaves out the bulky `raw` source blocks (often 10-30x smaller).

fields.name: fields
fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return, e.g. `posts.id,posts.title`. Call metadata is always included.

fresh.name: fresh
fresh.description: 1 skips the 24-hour cache and fetches live.

output.name: output
output.description: csv or ndjson returns the response's records (its main list, or the object as one row) as CSV or NDJSON instead of JSON.

records.name: records
records.description: With output=csv|ndjson: the top-level list to turn into rows (e.g. `reviews`), or `.` for the whole object as one row.

status_url.description: On a 503 for a paused endpoint: the status page, which lists open incidents.

E400.description: A parameter is missing or invalid. Not charged (unless the call ran and the source rejected the value; credits_used says).

E401.description: Missing, invalid, revoked or expired API key. Not charged. See https://api.sh/docs/errors#401

E402.description: Not enough credits, a spend limit you set was reached (`spend_limit`), or the key's monthly credit cap was reached (`key_cap`). Not charged.

E404.description: Not found, or not public. A lookup that ran costs the endpoint's price (credits_used says); an unknown route is free.

E502.description: The source site failed this time; retry. Not charged.

E503.description: Endpoint paused or temporarily unavailable; may include retry-after, and status_url (https://api.sh/status) for a paused endpoint. Not charged.
